import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bounds on fractional parts $n r^2 - a(n)$ for $r = (2+\sqrt{5})/2$

$a(n) = \lfloor r \cdot \lfloor r \cdot n \rfloor \rfloor$, where $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$.

*References:*
- [A341254](https://oeis.org/A341254)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA341254


open Real

/-- The constant $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$. -/
noncomputable def rConst : ℝ := (2 + sqrt 5) / 2

/-- The constant $r^2$. -/
noncomputable def rSq : ℝ := rConst * rConst

/--
$a(n) = \lfloor r \cdot \lfloor r \cdot n \rfloor \rfloor$, where $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$.
Note: The original OEIS definition has $n$ starting at 1. We define $a(n)$ for all $\mathbb{N}$.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let r := rConst
  let inner_floor : ℤ := Int.floor (r * n)
  (Int.floor (r * inner_floor.cast)).toNat


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 4 := by
  unfold a rConst
  dsimp only
  push_cast
  rw [mul_one]
  have h1 : ⌊(2 + Real.sqrt 5) / 2⌋ = 2 := by
    rw [Int.floor_eq_iff]
    have h5 : 2236 / 1000 < Real.sqrt 5 ∧ Real.sqrt 5 < 2237 / 1000 := by
      norm_num [Real.sqrt_lt, Real.lt_sqrt]
    constructor <;> linarith
  rw [h1]
  push_cast
  have h2 : ⌊(2 + Real.sqrt 5) / 2 * 2⌋ = 4 := by
    rw [Int.floor_eq_iff]
    have h5 : 2236 / 1000 < Real.sqrt 5 ∧ Real.sqrt 5 < 2237 / 1000 := by
      norm_num [Real.sqrt_lt, Real.lt_sqrt]
    constructor <;> linarith
  rw [h2]
  rfl

/--
Conjecture: $1/4 < n r^2 - a(n) < 3$ for $n \ge 1$, where $r = (2 + \sqrt{5})/2$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/341254.wip.lean#L188"]
theorem a_bounds (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : (1 / 4 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) * rSq - (a n : ℝ) ∧
    (n : ℝ) * rSq - (a n : ℝ) < 3 := by
    sorry

end OeisA341254

findings.description: The module title calls n r² − a(n) a “fractional part,” but it is an error from an iterated floor, not the fractional part of n r². For example, a(3) = 12 gives 3r² − a(3) = 3√5 − 21/4 > 1, whereas a fractional part is always less than 1. This inequality was verified in Lean. The definitions and bound theorem themselves are faithful to the source.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A341254 defines a(n) = floor(r*floor(r*n)) and states 1/4 < n*r² − a(n) < 3 for n ≥ 1. Its June 9, 2026 proof comment identifies eps = n*r − floor(n*r), not n*r² − a(n), as the fractional part. Read in the OEIS-maintained entry: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A341/A341254.seq.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the title to “Bounds on the double-floor error n r² − a(n)” or simply “Bounds on n r² − a(n).” Leave the mathematical declarations unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The sequence is represented as ℕ → ℕ, with the outer integer floor converted using Int.toNat and the definition extended to n = 0. OEIS gives the integer double-floor formula starting at n = 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since rConst ≥ 0 and n ≥ 0, both floor arguments and both integer floors are nonnegative. Thus Int.toNat preserves the outer floor exactly. Also rSq = rConst², and the theorem's hypothesis 1 ≤ n excludes the additional zero index. The scratch file proves the cast equality and a ↔ between the universally quantified Lean bounds and the literal source formula, without using a_bounds.

review.notes: Every declaration was checked; no substantive misformalization was found. The five test values agree with OEIS. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, an executable integer-square-root model was proved equal to a and matched all 10,000 b-file entries; exact square-based checks of both bounds passed on those indices. Lean also verified a(0) = 0 and failure of the lower bound at zero, which is correctly excluded. The research solved tag and existence-of-formal-proof record agree with OEIS's June 2026 proof comment and the cited literature. Direct OEIS entry pages returned HTTP 403, so the complete entry was read through its official data mirror.
